subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should OpenClaw change unconfigured `memorySearch.sync.intervalMinutes` from disabled to a default periodic fallback for this stale-index failure mode?
rationale: Root policy treats config defaults and fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive, and the open candidate PR needs explicit ownership of the upgrade tradeoff before this issue can close.

options.title: Approve default-on fallback after repair
options.body: Land the linked fix or a successor after scoping interval dirty marking to memory-source managers and accepting the 30-minute default as intended upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep periodic sync opt-in
options.body: Preserve the `0` default and make the documented workaround or doctor guidance the supported safety net for users who hit watcher outages.

options.title: Ask for watcher heartbeat design
options.body: Pause the periodic-default approach and require a liveness/heartbeat design if background rescan work is not an acceptable default.

recommendation.title: Approve default-on fallback after repair
recommendation.body: Land the linked fix or a successor after scoping interval dirty marking to memory-source managers and accepting the 30-minute default as intended upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily product/config-default direction, and recent memory-search config history points to this owner as the strongest decision route.
